Subject: Latency acceptance checks & next steps for SLO qualification (p95 / p99)

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick written recap so we have a single checklist to move to a short probe:

What we heard from you:
- Target e2e SLOs: p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 650ms for single-turn text completions under your typical traffic mix.
- Average request: ~160 tokens input + 80 tokens output (most responses are short).
- Concurrency profile: steady-state 150 rps, peaks up to ~480 rps for 30–90s bursts.
- Streaming is used in ~65% of calls; you rely on first-token latency for UX.

What Redwood will provide for the probe:
1) A short-run hosted probe that mirrors your traffic shape (prefix distribution + token lengths).
2) Per-request timing: client-to-redwood, redwood processing, and redwood-to-client (so we can map network vs processing).
3) p95/p99 reporting with raw sample export and per-route breakdown.
4) Streaming-enabled probe with chunking parameters to match your player.

Immediate asks / action items (owner in parentheses):
- Veridian: share a 15–minute representative traffic trace (anonymized) and example prompts (Samir)
- Veridian: confirm whether you’ll run the probe from your US region or want us to originate traffic from multiple regions (Priya)
- Redwood: provide probe instructions + latency-matrix template (Jonas / Ben) — attaching draft matrix now.
- Redwood: propose a 2-hour probe window next week and a follow-up review session (Laura).

Attachments: latency-matrix.csv (draft) and slo-probe-instructions.pdf (draft).

We'll avoid any production data in the initial run; the trace can be synthetic if you prefer. If you can send the trace and a preferred 2-hour window by EOD Monday I can lock in engineers and a probe runner.

Thanks — Jonas

Jonas — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The p95/p99 targets are for end-to-end user-visible latency (browser -> service -> model -> browser). Our current provider delivers ~p95=210ms / p99=720ms in our staging region under typical load; p99 spikes are the main concern.
- Streaming: our player expects chunked server-sent events every ~70 tokens; if chunk latency exceeds ~120ms users perceive a stall.
- Concurrency: 480 rps is an accurate short burst number during our nightly batch window — for the probe we are most concerned about 100–500 rps envelope.

We can provide an anonymized 20-minute trace from last week (will scrub identifiers). We prefer the probe traffic to originate from our US-east region first; happy to run an additional EU-based probe later.

Available windows next week: Tue 2027-03-23 09:00–11:00 ET or Wed 2027-03-24 13:00–15:00 ET. Please pick one and we’ll reserve an on-call SRE.

Also, please call out what network-level telemetry you need (tcpdump/pcap, SYN/ACK timestamps, or just TCP RTT samples).

—Samir

Samir — appreciate the windows. A few quick technical items so we can size the probe and make sure we measure the right things: 

1) Tokenization: are you using byte-pair encoding variants or sentencepiece for your client prompts? Send a sample prompt file so we can replicate token counts.
2) Streaming chunking: confirm you want ~70-token chunks; also tell us whether you use chunk-level ACKs in the player or simple append.
3) Concurrency shaping: do you want a steady ramp to 150 rps, then a stepped stress to 480 rps for 90s, or randomized bursts (Poisson)? We recommend a stepped profile for initial validation.
4) TLS termination and keepalive: will traffic terminate at our hosted API endpoint or behind your edge? For hosted probe please point traffic at our test endpoint; if you want us to instrument edge <-> redwood we can provide an nginx probe snippet.

Attached: latency-matrix.csv (populated with our baseline numbers) — please update the sampling buckets column with your observed breakdowns and return.

If you confirm Tue 2027-03-23 09:00–11:00 ET we’ll reserve an engineer and Karthik will draft a short SLA note describing acceptance criteria mapping to p95/p99 numbers.

Thanks,
